_comment: Mutation testing for the core CLI. Non-blocking (break: null) — run via
`npm run test:mutation` to surface a real mutation score, not as a CI gate.
WHY A TARGETED SCOPE: mutating all of src/**/*.ts is ~7k mutants and takes
hours, which nobody runs. The `mutate` list below is the subset where a
SURVIVING mutant is a safety problem rather than a cosmetic one — anything
that deletes files, decides what is skipped, builds a filesystem path, or
executes third-party code:
src/repairCommand.ts       (260 mutants) `repair --apply --prune` DELETES
local files. A survivor here means the prune
set can be wrong (deleting a claimed file, or
silently keeping an orphan) with no test noticing.
src/downloadCheckpoint.ts   (33 mutants) decides which tables a resumed
download SKIPS. A survivor means a stale
checkpoint is accepted and files are never
downloaded while the run reports success —
silent data loss, the exact bug the fingerprint
check was added to fix.
src/FileUtils.ts           (262 mutants) builds every local path and does
every read/write/delete on disk. Survivors here
are wrong-file / wrong-directory bugs.
src/genericUtils.ts        (108 mutants) owns the INJ-1 `isSafePathComponent`
path-traversal guard that FileUtils, the download
pipeline and the docs generator all rely on, plus
the chunking used to cap request fan-out.
src/PluginManager.ts        (78 mutants) resolves and executes third-party
plugin code in-process; survivors are
arbitrary-code-execution-shaped.
TOTAL IN SCOPE: 741 mutants, ~11 min wall clock on a 10-core machine.
READ THE TIMEOUT COUNT BEFORE READING THE SCORE: Stryker counts a TimedOut
mutant as DETECTED, on the theory that a mutant which hangs the suite was
caught by it. This package times out on roughly a quarter of its mutants for
reasons that have nothing to do with hanging, so every one of those is
silently added to the numerator and the score comes out OPTIMISTIC, not
conservative. The first full run timed out on 26.5% of 750 mutants, which
makes its "86.63%" really the band [60.0%, 86.63%] with the true value
unknown. Quote the band, not the number, until the timeouts are understood.
WHY THE BUDGET IS BACK AT THE DEFAULT: the timeouts were first blamed on slow
and variable ts-jest ESM startup under machine load, and the budget was raised
to timeoutMS 30000 / timeoutFactor 3 to compensate — roughly 2.7x the effective
per-mutant budget (timeoutMS + timeoutFactor * dryRunTime, so 30.5s -> 81s with
this package's ~17s dry run). That was measured and DISPROVEN: on an idle
machine the raised budget produced 70 timeouts in the first 262 mutants — 26.7%,
statistically identical to the 26.5% it was meant to fix. Neither `static` (6 vs
8) nor coverage breadth (10.6 vs 11.7 covering tests, 2.85 vs 2.58 covering test
FILES) separates Timeout from Killed. What does correlate is the mutated file —
48% of genericUtils.ts against 5% of repairCommand.ts. So the default is
restored: a budget that a mutant blows through at 2.7x is not a budget problem,
and the smaller value costs a healthy run nothing.
WHAT IS STILL OPEN: whether those timeouts are genuine hangs. The evidence cuts
both ways and neither side is settled. FOR real hangs: the timing-out mutators
are loop-shaped (50 ConditionalExpression, 38 BlockStatement, 24 EqualityOperator
— exactly the mutations that break a loop's termination), and both mutated files
are loop-heavy while repairCommand.ts is mostly linear. AGAINST: only 2 of 199
timeouts tripped Stryker's instrumented hit limit, which a loop through the
mutated statement should trip. Note the budget formula while reading any of this
— `timeoutFactor * netTime + timeoutMS + timeOverheadMS`, where under `perTest`
netTime counts only the COVERING tests, so a small pure function is budgeted at
little more than the constants. Do not restate the cause as settled without a
measurement; the earlier claim that StringLiteral and ArrayDeclaration mutants
"cannot loop" was wrong (`[]` -> `["Stryker was here"]` feeding a
drain-and-refill loop hangs perfectly well).
DELIBERATELY DEFERRED (measured, not forgotten): src/snClient.ts (733
mutants) and src/manifestBuilder.ts (738 mutants). Both are high value, but
together they triple the runtime to ~50 min, which pushes the run out of
"a developer will actually do this" territory. Widen by appending them to
`mutate` when there is time to triage ~200 more survivors.
